inventory_findings.message: D2/D5 sample-pass: tool-driven mechanics (Vale EN, LanguageTool DE) skipped by design; only LLM-driven D2 and D5 checks are active for this run.

findings.message: The term 'Task tool' is used without prior definition; for the non-operator audience 'downstream-user' it is unexplained Claude Code internal jargon on a published surface.
findings.evidence: Agents are dispatched by skills, or directly via the `Task` tool when the caller knows which agent it wants.
findings.suggested_resolution: Add a short parenthetical or footnote after first mention: 'the `Task` tool (a Claude Code API for dispatching agents programmatically)'.

findings.message: README serves 'downstream-user' (user-docs track) but is missing the required audience block: no section names the intended audiences by their audience-artefact IDs as mandated by docs-audience-tracks §User-docs content contract.
findings.evidence: No section in README.md enumerates audience IDs (e.g. 'downstream-user') or cites AUDIENCES.md as the source of truth for who the plugin is for.
findings.suggested_resolution: Add an '## Audiences' section (or expand '## Purpose') that names at minimum 'downstream-user' and 'dogfooding-author' with a reference to AUDIENCES.md.

findings.message: README serves 'downstream-user' (user-docs track) but is missing the required use-case/scenario block: there is no section naming the concrete functional scenarios the plugin is designed for, in end-user terms.
findings.evidence: The '## Purpose' section names the resource types (agents, skills, conventions) but does not enumerate concrete use-case scenarios or call out explicitly out-of-scope use cases.
findings.suggested_resolution: Add a '## Use cases' or '## When to use this plugin' section listing 3-5 concrete scenarios (e.g. 'enforce consistent PR workflow across a portfolio') and at least one explicit out-of-scope callout.

findings.message: Page declares 'track: developer-docs' in frontmatter but its audience includes 'downstream-user' whose canonical track is 'user-docs'; this is an audience-to-track contradiction for a non-operator audience.
findings.evidence: Frontmatter: track: developer-docs — audience: [maintainer, downstream-user]. AUDIENCES.md maps 'downstream-user' to track: user-docs.
findings.suggested_resolution: Change 'track: developer-docs' to 'track: user-docs', or split into two pages: one for downstream-user (user-docs) and one for maintainer (developer-docs).

findings.message: Page declares 'track: developer-docs' in frontmatter but its audience includes 'downstream-user' whose canonical track is 'user-docs'; this is an audience-to-track contradiction for a non-operator audience.
findings.evidence: Frontmatter: track: developer-docs — audience: [maintainer, downstream-user]. AUDIENCES.md maps 'downstream-user' to track: user-docs.
findings.suggested_resolution: Change 'track: developer-docs' to 'track: user-docs', or split into two pages: one for downstream-user (user-docs) and one for maintainer (developer-docs).

findings.message: The phrase 'token efficiency' is unexplained jargon from LLM infrastructure; it is not part of the base vocabulary for 'downstream-user' and appears without definition on a published how-to page.
findings.evidence: Skill files themselves are kept in English (token efficiency).
findings.suggested_resolution: Replace with a plain-language explanation, e.g. 'Skill files are written in English to keep Claude's processing cost low; Claude still detects your language and replies in it.'

findings.message: Step 1 instructs the reader to 'read the spec first' but provides no link or path to where specs live; for 'external-contributor' this is a hidden prerequisite on a how-to page.
findings.evidence: **Spec zuerst lesen** — Skill oder Agent folgt immer einer geltenden Spezifikation.
findings.suggested_resolution: Add a link to spec/README.md or ../references/specs/index.md so an external contributor knows where to find the specs before starting.

findings.message: Step 2 instructs the reader to invoke the skill-management skill but provides no instruction on how to load the plugin; for 'external-contributor' this is a hidden prerequisite on a how-to page.
findings.evidence: **Skill/Agent anlegen** — nutze den Skill-Management-Skill. Er scaffolden ASCII-Kebab-Case-Ordner…
findings.suggested_resolution: Add a prerequisites section at the top linking to the plugin installation instructions (README.md §Usage) before the workflow steps begin.

findings.message: The abbreviation 'SLA' is used without expansion; it does not appear in the first paragraph or a heading but is visible in a published artefact targeting all audiences.
findings.evidence: **No SLA.** Skills and agents are best-effort automation.
findings.suggested_resolution: Expand on first use: 'No SLA (service-level agreement).' or rephrase as 'No service-level agreement.'.

findings.message: The 'Workflow cascade constraint' note contains operator-internal CI plumbing details (GITHUB_TOKEN, automerge.yaml, release-drafter.yml) irrelevant to 'downstream-user'; this is wrong-audience content in a README that serves every audience.
findings.evidence: GitHub Actions doesn't cascade workflow runs from events produced by a GITHUB_TOKEN-authenticated step… release-drafter.yml doesn't fire after an automerge.yaml squash-merge…
findings.suggested_resolution: flag-for-operator-move: move this note to a developer-docs page (e.g. docs/en/guides/contributing.md or a dedicated CI-caveats page) and replace it with a one-liner in the README pointing there.

findings.message: The term 'Plugin-Prefix' is used without prior definition; for 'downstream-user' this is unexplained jargon on a how-to page.
findings.evidence: Skills des Plugins sind per Name aufrufbar — optional mit Plugin-Prefix:
findings.suggested_resolution: Expand inline: 'optional mit Plugin-Prefix (z. B. /nolte-shared:spec anstatt nur /spec):'

findings.message: The term 'Runtime-Location' is used without prior definition; for 'maintainer' audience this is an unexplained hybrid English/German technical term.
findings.evidence: für den /skills-Dialog zusätzlich eine Runtime-Location (typischerweise per Symlink) nötig ist.
findings.suggested_resolution: Replace with a defined German term or add an inline expansion: 'eine Runtime-Location (Pfad, unter dem Claude Code den Skill zur Laufzeit findet, typischerweise ein Symlink nach ~/.claude/skills/<name>/)'

findings.message: The term 'Kanon (EN)' is used as a project-internal concept without prior definition; for 'external-contributor' this is unexplained insider jargon.
findings.evidence: der Kanon (EN) ist die Wahrheit, alles andere wird aus ihm regeneriert.
findings.suggested_resolution: Add a one-sentence definition on first use: 'der englische Kanon (die maßgebliche EN-Quelldatei, aus der alle Übersetzungen generiert werden)'.
